name: John Wrawe
role: Chaplain; leader of the Suffolk rising
description: A chaplain who led the rising as it spread north from Essex into Suffolk in mid-June 1381. His forces stormed Bury St Edmunds Abbey; Prior John Cambridge fled but was caught two days later and beheaded, and Sir John Cavendish -- Chief Justice and Chancellor of the University of Cambridge -- was tracked down at Lakenheath and killed. After the revolt's collapse Wrawe was captured, tried in London, and gave evidence against roughly two dozen associates in an apparent bid for clemency; he was executed anyway, by hanging, drawing, and quartering, on 6 May 1382.
narrative_function: Carries the revolt's East Anglian phase; his post-capture testimony is a rare window into the rising's internal organization.
